latest.content:
Today 07:00
RNS Number : 1386U
Futura Medical PLC
10 September 2026
10 September 2026
Futura Medical plc
("Futura" or the "Company")
Board Change
Futura Medical plc (AIM: FUM), the consumer healthcare group behind Eroxon®, that specialises in the development and global commercialisation of innovative and clinically proven sexual health products, announces that Roy Davis has informed the Company of his decision to step down from his role as Non-Executive Director with effect from 20
th
October 2026.
Roy’s decision follows a review of his wider board commitments and the time required to fulfil them. With a number of other board responsibilities, Roy has concluded that this is the appropriate time to step down from the Futura Board. His decision is unrelated to the Company’s business, performance or prospects, and he remains strongly supportive of Futura and its current strategy.
Following Roy's departure, the Board will consist of Andrew Unitt (Chair), Alexander Duggan (Chief Executive Officer), Angela Hildreth (COO and Finance Director) and Ken James (Head of R&D). The board has given careful consideration to its composition and, given the Company's current position, the Board does not intend to appoint a replacement Non-Executive Director at this time. The Board will monitor its composition and governance requirements carefully.
Andrew Unitt, Chair of Futura, commented:
"On behalf of the Board, I would like to thank Roy for his outstanding contribution to Futura. His experience, insight and advice have been invaluable during an important period in the Company's development. While we are sorry to see him step down, we fully understand his decision as part of a long-planned review of his wider board and time commitments, and we are pleased that he remains strongly supportive of Futura."

Notes to Editors:
Futura Medical plc (AIM: FUM) is the developer of innovative, consumer-focused, sexual health products, including lead product Eroxon® and development projects WSD4000 and Eroxon® Intense. Our core strength lies in our research, development, regulatory and business development expertise in developing innovative, clinically proven, insight-led and effective products to support our customers in the growing sexual health market.
Sexual health issues are prevalent globally in both men and women. Erectile Dysfunction ("
ED
") impacts 1 in 5 men globally across all adult age brackets, with approximately half of all men over 40 experiencing ED and 25% of all new diagnoses being in men under 40. 60% of women experience at least one symptom of impaired sexual response or function in a twelve-month period, with only one in four women seeking professional help and remaining chronically underserved.
Eroxon®, Futura's clinically proven lead product, has been developed for the treatment of ED. The highly differentiated product, which is the only topical gel treatment for ED available over the counter and helps men get an erection fast, addresses significant unmet needs in the ED market. Multiple license or distribution partnerships are in place for Eroxon®, across major consumer markets.
WSD4000 is a project name for Futura's development female sexual health portfolio, starting with the creation of a range of topical gels under Futura's unique platform technology, specifically designed to treat symptoms of sexual dysfunction in women. There is currently no known regulatory approved OTC treatment available for impaired sexual response and function in women. WSD4000 has the potential to be an effective, breakthrough treatment for the common symptoms associated with impaired sexual response and function, such as lack of desire, arousal, lubrication, ability to orgasm and overall sexual satisfaction.

Disclosure requirements of the Takeover Code
Under Rule 8.3(a) of the Code, any person who is interested in 1% or more of any class of relevant securities of an offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror (being any offeror other than an offeror in respect of which it has been announced that its offer is, or is likely to be, solely in cash) must make an Opening Position Disclosure following the commencement of the offer period and, if later, following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. An Opening Position Disclosure must contain details of the person's interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s). An Opening Position Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(a) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the commencement of the offer period and, if appropriate, by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. Relevant persons who deal in the relevant securities of the offeree company or of a securities exchange offeror prior to the deadline for making an Opening Position Disclosure must instead make a Dealing Disclosure.
Under Rule 8.3(b) of the Code, any person who is, or becomes, interested in 1% or more of any class of relevant securities of the offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror must make a Dealing Disclosure if the person deals in any relevant securities of the offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror. A Dealing Disclosure must contain details of the dealing concerned and of the person's interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s), save to the extent that these details have previously been disclosed under Rule 8. A Dealing Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(b) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the business day following the date of the relevant dealing.
If two or more persons act together pursuant to an agreement or understanding, whether formal or informal, to acquire or control an interest in relevant securities of an offeree company or a securities exchange offeror, they will be deemed to be a single person for the purpose of Rule 8.3.
Opening Position Disclosures must also be made by the offeree company and by any offeror and Dealing Disclosures must also be made by the offeree company, by any offeror and by any persons acting in concert with any of them (see Rules 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4).
Details of the offeree and offeror companies in respect of whose relevant securities Opening Position Disclosures and Dealing Disclosures must be made can be found in the Disclosure Table on the Takeover Panel's website at
www.thetakeoverpanel.org.uk
, including details of the number of relevant securities in issue, when the offer period commenced and when any offeror was first identified. You should contact the Panel's Market Surveillance Unit on +44 (0)20 7638 0129 if you are in any doubt as to whether you are required to make an Opening Position Disclosure or a Dealing Disclosure.

company_30s.what_they_do: Futura Medical plc (ticker FUM.L) develops and commercialises novel therapeutic technologies for chronic pain and inflammatory conditions, focusing on a proprietary drug delivery platform called Eroxon® that delivers small‑molecule drugs directly to target tissues.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The chronic pain market is a multi‑billion‑pound industry with limited effective options. Futura’s platform promises faster onset, reduced side‑effects and lower costs than existing systemic therapies, positioning it to capture a sizable share of the unmet need for safer pain management.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a late‑stage development phase, having recently secured a U.S. commercial partnership and cleared a European market launch. It is still burning cash as it ramps up clinical studies and prepares for an upcoming retail offering, but it is no longer a pre‑revenue start‑up.

rns_narrative: The first theme is a strategic pivot from pure R&D to monetisation: the company is raising capital, launching a retail offer and positioning itself for a merger or acquisition process to accelerate product commercialization.

The second theme is clinical momentum: new study data for its flagship WSD4000 compound show encouraging efficacy signals, and a European patent opposition has been resolved in its favour, securing intellectual‑property protection for the Eroxon® platform.
The third theme is corporate governance: board changes and a formal notice of general meeting suggest a tightening of executive oversight, likely in preparation for a larger capital raise.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet but cautious optimism – traders are watching for the next big announcement.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Some bullish voices point to the fresh U.S. partnership and the positive study results as a sign that the platform is finally on track to deliver real revenue streams.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bearish chatter focuses on the heavy cash burn, the fact that the company has not yet generated sales, and the risk that the retail offer could fail to meet expectations.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The tone has shifted from pure skepticism to a more measured wait‑and‑see stance; people are still reluctant to commit capital but are keeping an eye on the next earnings or partnership update.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends are flat – there is no public search activity, so any substantive news will hit like a shockwave.

near_term_catalysts: A formal announcement of the retail offer’s subscription results – a successful raise would signal investor confidence and provide the liquidity needed for product launch.
Publication of the full WSD4000 study data or a regulatory filing in the U.S. that clears the drug for human trials – a clear step toward revenue.
A board‑approved milestone in the European patent opposition process that confirms the company’s intellectual‑property rights.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sudden spike in trading volume paired with a break above the 20‑day moving average. A clear uptick in institutional buying after the retail offer announcement would confirm that smart money is stepping in.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the late stage of capitulation – the price has already fallen far below its pre‑crash level and the market has largely moved on. The APEX score suggests a tight compression, so the next move could be a sharp rebound once a catalyst lands.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the retail offer closes successfully and the company delivers the promised study data, the price could recover to roughly half of its pre‑crash level. That would represent a 50% upside from today’s price, a return that exceeds the historical average for RED signals and is consistent with the 162.8% mean return seen in the most dramatic bounces.
